en.t: I had almost forgotten the word “junshi,” dying in loyalty to one’s lord.

units.source_text: 因为平时用不上，所以沉淀在记忆的底层，似乎快要腐烂了，

en.t: Because it was not used in ordinary life, it had sunk to the bottom of my memory and seemed almost to be rotting there,

units.source_text: 听到妻的调侃，我才想起它来。

en.t: and only when I heard my wife’s joking remark did I remember it.

units.source_text: 我回答妻子，倘若真能殉死的话，我就准备为明治精神殉死。

en.t: I answered my wife that, if I could truly commit junshi, I would be prepared to die for the spirit of Meiji.

units.source_text: 当然，我的回答也不过是个玩笑，

en.t: Of course, my answer too was no more than a joke,

units.source_text: 但那时，我似乎感觉到这个陈腐不堪的词，被赋予了新的含意。

en.t: but at that moment I seemed to feel that this utterly worn-out word had been given a new meaning.

units.source_text: 过了一个月左右，在天皇大葬之夜，我像往常一样坐在书房中，聆听着丧礼的炮声。

en.t: About a month later, on the night of the Emperor’s state funeral, I sat in my study as usual and listened to the funeral cannon.

units.source_text: 我觉得那炮声，犹如在宣布明治时代一去不复返了。

en.t: To me, those cannon shots sounded as if they were announcing that the Meiji era had gone forever.

units.source_text: 后来才想到，这炮声也成了乃木大将永辞人世的讣告。

en.t: Only later did I realize that those shots had also become the obituary announcing General Nogi’s departure from this world.

units.source_text: 我拿着号外，忍不住对妻子说：‘殉死吧！殉死吧！’

en.t: Holding the newspaper extra in my hand, I could not help saying to my wife, “Junshi! Junshi!”

units.source_text: 我在报上读到了乃木大将临死前写下的遗书，

en.t: In the newspaper I read the testament that General Nogi had written before his death,

units.source_text: 其中有一段话大致意思是：自从西南战争时被敌人夺去军旗以来，一直想要以死谢罪，却苟活到了今天。

en.t: and in it was a passage to the effect that, ever since the enemy had taken his regimental flag during the Satsuma Rebellion, he had wanted to atone with his death, yet had gone on living until that day.

units.source_text: 读到这段时，我不由得屈指算了算乃木先生决心一死却活到今天是多少年。

en.t: When I read that passage, I could not help counting on my fingers how many years Mr. Nogi had lived on after resolving to die.

units.source_text: 西南战争爆发在明治十年，所以到明治四十五年时，相隔了三十五年之久。

en.t: The Satsuma Rebellion broke out in the tenth year of Meiji, so by the forty-fifth year of Meiji, thirty-five years had passed.

units.source_text: 由此看来，在这三十五年当中，乃木先生一直等待着死的时机。

en.t: Seen in that light, throughout those thirty-five years Mr. Nogi had been waiting for the right moment to die.

units.source_text: 我想，对他来说，是活三十五年痛苦呢，还是把刀刺入胸中的一刹那间痛苦呢？

en.t: I wondered which was more painful for him: living through those thirty-five years, or the single instant when he thrust the blade into his breast?
